test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 4 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A dog sees a cat at a distance of 280 m. The cat immediately runs away at a speed of 10 km/h and the dog also runs after it at a speed of 24 km/h to catch it. How much time will the dog take to catch the cat?
solution:
**Given:**

Distance between the dog and the cat = 280 m

Speed of the cat = 10 km/h

Speed of the dog = 24 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

Relative Speed = Speed of the dog - Speed of the cat

Relative Speed = 24 km/h - 10 km/h

Relative Speed = 14 km/h

Convert 14 km/h to m/s:

14 km/h = 14 × (5/18) = 3.89 m/s

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

Time = 280 m / 3.89 m/s

⇒ Time = 72 s

Convert 72 seconds to minutes:

1 minute = 60 seconds

Time = 72 s × (1)/(60)

⇒ Time = 1.2 min

**The dog will take 1.2 minutes to catch the cat.**
